html:
Autumn 2026 is an ideal season to explore the ancient and romantic charm of Hoi An. With mild weather, gentle sunshine, and fewer crowds, travelers can leisurely wander lantern-lit streets, visit historic landmarks, and enjoy the city’s rich culinary heritage.

Recognized as a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site, Hoi An captivates visitors with its well-preserved ancient town, glowing lanterns, traditional craft villages, and distinctive cuisine. Unlike the vibrant energy of summer or the quiet calm of winter, autumn brings a soft, poetic beauty that allows travelers to experience Hoi An at a slower, more meaningful pace.

Autumn in Hoi An typically lasts from September to November, with average temperatures ranging from 25–30°C. The pleasant climate is perfect for outdoor exploration. On full-moon nights, electric lights are turned off throughout the Old Town and replaced by thousands of lanterns, creating a magical and dreamlike atmosphere that leaves a lasting impression on every visitor.

Must Visit Attractions And Experiences In Hoi An During Autumn 2026

1. Hoi An Lantern Streets – A Magical Nighttime Experience

Lanterns are the soul of Hoi An. As night falls, colorful lanterns illuminate streets, alleys, and ancient houses, creating a romantic and unforgettable scene. Autumn’s cool air enhances the charm, making evening walks especially enjoyable.

Visitors can take a small wooden boat along the Hoai River, release floating lanterns, and admire the glowing Old Town from the water. Lantern-making workshops are also popular, allowing travelers to create their own handmade souvenir inspired by local culture.

2. Ba Mu Temple Gate (Tam Quan Ba Mu) – Ancient Architecture In The Heart Of The Old Town

The Tam Quan Ba Mu Gate is a striking historical structure known for its elegant design and peaceful surroundings. Restored with care, it features a tranquil pond, green lawns, and impressive architectural details that reflect Hoi An’s cultural depth. Autumn brings a calm and serene atmosphere, ideal for photography and quiet reflection.

3. Japanese Covered Bridge – A Cultural Icon Of Hoi An

Also known as Chua Cau, this iconic bridge symbolizes the cultural exchange between Vietnam and Japan during Hoi An’s trading-port era. Its curved roof, intricate carvings, and spiritual significance make it one of the most photographed landmarks in the city. Soft autumn sunlight highlights its timeless beauty.

4. Abandoned Brick Kiln – A Unique Photo Spot

Located about 5 kilometers from the Old Town, an abandoned brick kiln surrounded by rice fields has become a favorite destination for photography enthusiasts. Its raw, rustic appearance contrasts beautifully with the blue autumn sky, offering dramatic and artistic photo opportunities. Sunrise and sunset are the best times to visit.

5. Hoai River – Poetic And Peaceful

Flowing gently through the Old Town, the Hoai River adds a poetic touch to Hoi An’s scenery. In the evening, lantern reflections shimmer on the water as boats glide quietly along. Riverside cafés provide perfect spots to relax, enjoy Vietnamese coffee, and watch life unfold at a slow pace.

6. Thanh Ha Pottery Village – Preserving Traditional Craftsmanship

Situated along the Thu Bon River, Thanh Ha Pottery Village offers insight into centuries-old ceramic traditions. Visitors can watch skilled artisans at work or try shaping pottery themselves. The village’s rustic charm and cultural authenticity make it a meaningful stop for travelers interested in local heritage.

7. Bay Mau Coconut Forest – A “Mini Mekong” Experience

This lush water coconut forest offers a completely different perspective of Hoi An. Guests ride basket boats through narrow waterways, watch traditional fishing demonstrations, and enjoy lively local performances. Autumn’s cooler temperatures make this eco-experience especially comfortable.

8. An Bang And Cua Dai Beaches – Tranquility By The Sea

For those seeking relaxation, An Bang and Cua Dai beaches offer quiet escapes from the Old Town. In autumn, the beaches are peaceful, ideal for seaside walks, watching sunrise or sunset, and enjoying fresh seafood in beachfront restaurants.

9. Fujian Assembly Hall – Chinese Architectural Heritage

This grand assembly hall showcases traditional Chinese architecture with ornate gates, courtyards, and altars dedicated to sea deities. It reflects the historical presence of the Chinese community in Hoi An and is an excellent place to learn about the city’s multicultural past.

10. Tan Ky Ancient House – Living History

Over 200 years old, Tan Ky Ancient House beautifully blends Vietnamese, Japanese, and Chinese architectural elements. Visiting this well-preserved home offers insight into the lifestyle and trading history of Hoi An’s merchant families.

11. Traditional Craft Workshops – Art And Heritage

Hoi An is home to numerous craft workshops producing lanterns, silk, leather goods, and woodwork. Visitors can observe artisans at work, purchase handmade souvenirs, or join short workshops to create personalized keepsakes.

12. Cu Lao Cham Islands – A Natural Paradise

About 15 kilometers offshore, the Cu Lao Cham Islands feature pristine beaches, coral reefs, and traditional fishing villages. Autumn seas are calm, making it a great time for snorkeling, swimming, and enjoying fresh seafood. The islands are recognized as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.

13. Hoi An Night Market – Local Flavors And Shopping

As night falls, the night market along the Hoai River becomes lively with lantern stalls, street food vendors, and souvenir shops. It is the perfect place to sample local snacks, shop for handmade items, and experience the vibrant nightlife of Hoi An.

Hoi An Autumn Cuisine – Flavors You Should Not Miss

No trip to Hoi An is complete without tasting its iconic dishes, including:

  • Cao Lau – Thick noodles with roasted pork and fresh herbs

  • Mi Quang – Turmeric noodles with rich but light broth

  • Hoi An Chicken Rice – Fragrant rice with shredded chicken

  • Banh Mi Phuong – Famous Vietnamese baguette

  • White Rose Dumplings – Delicate shrimp-filled dumplings

  • Herbal “Mot” Drink – Refreshing traditional beverage

Travel Tips For Visiting Hoi An In Autumn 2026

  • Book accommodation early, as autumn is a popular travel season

  • Explore the Old Town on foot or by bicycle

  • Bring light layers for cooler evenings

  • Carry some cash for local markets

  • Respect local culture and protect the environment

Final Thoughts

Hoi An in autumn 2026 offers a perfect blend of history, culture, cuisine, and tranquil beauty. From lantern-lit streets and ancient architecture to peaceful rivers and traditional villages, every moment feels poetic and unforgettable. Whether you are a culture lover, a food enthusiast, or a photography fan, Hoi An promises a deeply rewarding journey.
